question: Is the closed-form solve already near its own optimum in the objective it actually minimizes (value/attention-space MSE), while token cross-entropy barely moves?
variable_under_test: fitting freedom: (a) TOP_T=32 + RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4 (canonical) vs (b) TOP_T=512 (=all 511 slots) + RIDGE_LAMBDA=0 (MSE->0 oracle); all other knobs held identical

observations: Run (a) reproduced the canonical best gradient-free point EXACTLY: QA 2.1766157150268555 / MT 2.5483615398406982, bit-identical to EXP-007-top32 to every printed digit, on a different GPU in a fresh process and through a different import path (frozen package snapshot vs EXP-007's sibling-repo install); value_global_max_abs (984.0) and mean_mse_last_doc (0.198077) also matched exactly, so the harness and the top32 operating point are confirmed stable. At that operating point the solve's own objective is already small in absolute terms: mean am/mean_mse over the 16 documents is 0.1191 (first doc 0.0085, last 0.1981), and per-layer on the last document 34 of 36 layers sit at or below 0.156 with a median near 0.0027 - 93.0% of the total per-layer MSE lives in just layers 34 and 35 (4.40 and 2.23). Run (b) gave the solve maximal fitting freedom - TOP_T=512, which the ranker clamps to all 511 trainable slots per layer (16x run (a)'s support), with RIDGE_LAMBDA=0 taking the unregularized torch.linalg.lstsq branch - and it ran to completion in 234s with no OOM, so no fallback to TOP_T=256 was needed. That extra freedom lowered the solve's own error by 23.1% (mean am/mean_mse 0.1191 -> 0.0915; the reduction is consistent across all 16 documents, ratio 0.62-0.85) yet MT acquisition moved the WRONG WAY, from 2.5484 to 2.6652 (+0.117), while QA forgetting degraded from 2.1766 to 2.5151 (+0.339) as expected from the larger footprint; the standalone eval_forgetting.py runs on the saved cache_last.pt checkpoints agree with the in-run evals to within 0.004 (a: QA 2.1772 / MT 2.5524; b: QA 2.5133 / MT 2.6630). The oracle did NOT reach MSE~0: DELTA_WEIGHT was held at 1e-2 per the task spec, and that trust-region term appends a 511x511 identity block to the stacked design matrix, so the system stays over-determined even with every slot free and the residual is floored - and the part that does not shrink is exactly layers 34/35 (ratios 0.93x and 0.77x), which still carry 95.4% of the residual in run (b), while the other 34 layers drop 44.5%. Noise caveat: the eval splits are a handful of batches (QA n=6, MT n=5) and there is no knob to enlarge them, so sub-0.1-0.2 loss deltas are noise; the MT change here (+0.117) sits at the edge of that band and is therefore best read as 'MT did not improve' rather than as a confirmed regression, whereas the QA change (+0.339) and the MSE change (-23%, uniform across all 16 documents) are outside it. Provenance: both runs used a frozen PYTHONPATH-pinned snapshot of the cartridges package taken before either run; the concurrent ORACLE-WRITE worker edited the driver on the live tree during run (a), but its AM_ORACLE_WRITE block is opt-in and conditional on the imported package exposing an oracle_write field, which the frozen snapshot does not, so it contributed {} and neither run's config.yaml contains that field; more importantly the same worker also edited cartridges/am/value_solve.py (19:22:42), finetune.py (19:23:12) and continual.py (19:23:37) on the live tree while run (a) was still loading the model, and the frozen snapshot - verified byte-identical to committed git HEAD and hash-unchanged after both runs - is what both of my runs actually executed.
